title: The yogis' earrings
hookLine: the yogis offer Nanak their earrings, bag and patched coat; he names what he'd wear instead

lines: A RING THAT DOESN'T COME OFF.
cards: A ring through the ear is hard to take off. The yogis Nanak met wore earrings as a mark of their order, and tradition says the ring marked an initiation, a road a person had chosen for good.

Add a shoulder bag and a coat stitched together from patches, and the look was unmistakable. In the Sidh Gosht they make Nanak an offer: take on our look, our earrings, our bag, our patched coat. Join us.

teach.h: OUR PATH IS BEST, THE YOGIS SAY.
teach.b: It's a generous offer, made with pride: our path is the best of the yogic paths, the yogis say, in paraphrase. Nanak doesn't mock the earrings. He takes each piece and moves it inside.

teach.h: THE WORD IS THE EARRING, WITHIN.
teach.b: His answer, in paraphrase: let the Word, the shabad, be the earring, worn within, never taken out. Clear away ego and the grip of mine.
Let go of lust, anger and pride, and through the Guru's Word, real understanding comes.

teach.h: THE COAT: THE ONE IN EVERYTHING.
teach.b: And for the patched coat and the bag: see the Lord filling everything. The One, Nanak says, carries a person across. Look at what he kept.
He kept the idea of the earring: something worn always, a mark of who you belong to, a sign you aren't going back. He just put it where nobody can see it.
The yogi's ring is in the ear; Nanak's is in what the ear keeps hearing. The coat too.

teach.h: IT CATCHES THE LIGHT ALL DAY.
teach.b: The yogi's coat is made of scraps sewn together. Nanak's is the whole world, with the One stitched through every piece. There's an echo from the Japji, where he gave the yogis earrings of contentment.
Here, the earring is the Word itself. Think about what an earring does all day. You forget it's there.
Then you catch it in a mirror, or it brushes your neck when you turn your head, and you remember.
That's one way to picture what the stanza asks of the Word: a line of Gurbani that keeps catching the light through an ordinary day, bringing you back.

how: Sikhs do not take on the yogis' earrings or patched coat; the Sidh Gosht's answer is read as moving those outward marks inward, and some keep a line of Gurbani in mind through the day as a way of wearing the Word.

o: marks of the yogis' order, which Nanak moved inside as the Word
ornaments Sikhs wear as one of the five articles of faith
a gift of gold the yogis offered Nanak to stay with them

games.q: the yogis' gear and Nanak's — tap the pairs.

s: he keeps the idea of the earring and moves it inside: the Word becomes the earring.
in the Sidh Gosht, the earring Nanak names is the Word
let the shabad within be the earring, he says.
Sikhs wear the yogis' patched coat as a sign of the Word
Nanak's patched coat is seeing the One filling everything, not a garment.

games.q: the yogis offer you their earrings, bag and patched coat, the marks of their order. what does Nanak do with the offer?
o: put them on to keep the peace.
name an inner earring and coat instead.
games.why: he answers piece by piece: the Word is the earring, and seeing the One everywhere is the coat and the bag.

practice: Choose one short line you've met on this path, a line of Gurbani, the word Waheguru, or today's line itself, and imagine fastening it in place the way you'd put on an earring in the morning.
Then let it go quiet, and every few breaths let it catch the light again; if the mind wanders, that's fine, since an earring is easy to forget, and each time you notice, you've found it again.
If you pray, the line you chose can be the prayer, worn quietly.

wordCard.voice: The yogis' earrings. Their offer of earrings, bag and patched coat, and Nanak's answer: let the Word be the earring, and the One in everything be the coat. Today's word.

orig.note: mundra: the yogi's earring, which Nanak's answer turns into the Word worn within.

carryVoice: Your line: the word as earring. Worn within, it catches the light all day. I'll be here tomorrow.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ramkali, Mahala 1, Sidh Gosht, pauris 9–10, Ang 939 (the yogis' offer; the Word as earring; the coat and bag)
Guru Granth Sahib, Japji, pauri 28, Ang 6 (earrings of contentment)
